# help showfilesystem
showfilesystem - Display information of all filesystems or a specific filesystem in a system.

SYNTAX
    showfilesystem [name]

DESCRIPTION
    The showfilesystem command displays information about all the filesystems
    or a specific filesystem in a system.

AUTHORITY
    Any role in the system

OPTIONS
    -space
        Displays the filesystem space usage.

    -state
        Lists the detailed state information of filesystem and
        the underlying VV.

    -d
        Lists the detailed information of filesystem.

    -vv
        Lists the information of the VV on which filesystems are created.

    -allnames
        Shows both the shortened and full filesystem names.

    -notree
        Do not display filesystem names in tree format.

    -snapsched
        Lists all the schedules associated with the filesystem.

    -snap
        Displays all the filesystems in the snapshot tree for the specified
        base filesystem.

    -hist
        Displays the history information of the filesystems.
        The following columns are shown:
        Id Name Prov Type CreationTime RetentionEndTime ExpirationTime

    -retained
        Displays filesystems that have a retention time.

    -expired
        Displays the filesystems that have expired.

SPECIFIERS
    <name>
        Specifies the filesystem name whose information will be displayed.
        If not specified, configuration information for all filesystems in
        the system is displayed.

NOTES
    Long names can cause the display to be very wide. Use -shortnames
    to display shortened 31 character names for objects. Use the setclienv
    command to set shortnames to 1. The -shortnames option is also set to 1
    if the CLI was started with the -shortnames option, or if the CLI was
    started with the TPDSHORTNAMES environment variable set. Run "cli -h"
    and "setclienv -h" for details of the environment variables.

EXAMPLES
    The following example shows all the filesystems on the system.

       cli% showfilesystem

    The following example shows demo_fs filesystem on the system.

       cli% showfilesystem demo_fs
